warmup.why: Counting starts at 0, so [1] is the second thing. You'll need that in about twenty minutes.

riddle.q: Nine coins look the same. One is a little heavier. You have a balance scale. What's the fewest weighings that always finds it?
riddle.a: Two. Weigh three against three. If one side drops, the heavy coin is in it. If they balance, it's in the three you left out. Then weigh one against one from that group.

meetings.title: Remember what they did
meetings.leave_with: A character who treats you differently the second time you talk to them.

warmup.why: in asks whether something is on a list. That one word is most of today.

riddle.q: Three switches downstairs. One of them works the bulb upstairs, and you can't see the bulb from here. Flip them all you want, but you only get one trip up. How do you find the right switch?
riddle.a: Turn the first one on for a few minutes, then turn it off and turn the second one on. Go up. If the bulb is on, it's the second. If it's off and warm, the first. Off and cold, the third.

warmup.why: A function is a block with a name. Every part of your island is one.

riddle.q: Two doors, two guards. One guard always lies and one always tells the truth, and you don't know which is which. One door is the way out. You get one question for one guard. What do you ask?
riddle.a: Ask either one: which door would the other guard say is the way out? Then take the opposite door.
